# Data Source: stripe_mandate

A customer's authorization to charge a payment method. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_setup_intent" "sepa" {
  id = "seti_123"
}

data "stripe_mandate" "sepa" {
  id = data.stripe_setup_intent.sepa.mandate
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

Exactly one must be set.

* `id` - (Optional) Unique identifier for the object.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `customer_acceptance` - See [`customer_acceptance`](#customer_acceptance) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `multi_use` - See [`multi_use`](#multi_use) below.
* `on_behalf_of` - The account (if any) that the mandate is intended for.
* `payment_method` - ID of the payment method associated with this mandate.
* `payment_method_details` - See [`payment_method_details`](#payment_method_details) below.
* `single_use` - See [`single_use`](#single_use) below.
* `status` - The mandate status indicates whether or not you can use it to initiate a payment. Possible values: `active`, `inactive`, `pending`.
* `type` - The type of the mandate. Possible values: `multi_use`, `single_use`.

<a id="customer_acceptance"></a>
### `customer_acceptance`

The `customer_acceptance` attribute supports:

* `accepted_at` - The time that the customer accepts the mandate.
* `online` - See [`customer_acceptance.online`](#customer_acceptance.online) below.
* `type` - The mandate includes the type of customer acceptance information, such as: `online` or `offline`. Possible values: `offline`, `online`.

<a id="customer_acceptance.online"></a>
### `customer_acceptance.online`

The `customer_acceptance.online` attribute supports:

* `ip_address` - The customer accepts the mandate from this IP address.
* `user_agent` - The customer accepts the mandate using the user agent of the browser.

<a id="multi_use"></a>
### `multi_use`

The `multi_use` attribute supports:

* `amount` - The amount of the payment on a multi use mandate.
* `currency` - The currency of the payment on a multi use mandate.

<a id="payment_method_details"></a>
### `payment_method_details`

The `payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `acss_debit` - See [`payment_method_details.acss_debit`](#payment_method_details.acss_debit) below.
* `au_becs_debit` - See [`payment_method_details.au_becs_debit`](#payment_method_details.au_becs_debit) below.
* `bacs_debit` - See [`payment_method_details.bacs_debit`](#payment_method_details.bacs_debit) below.
* `blik` - See [`payment_method_details.blik`](#payment_method_details.blik) below.
* `card` - See [`payment_method_details.card`](#payment_method_details.card) below.
* `paypal` - See [`payment_method_details.paypal`](#payment_method_details.paypal) below.
* `payto` - See [`payment_method_details.payto`](#payment_method_details.payto) below.
* `pix` - See [`payment_method_details.pix`](#payment_method_details.pix) below.
* `sepa_debit` - See [`payment_method_details.sepa_debit`](#payment_method_details.sepa_debit) below.
* `type` - This mandate corresponds with a specific payment method type. The `payment_method_details` includes an additional hash with the same name and contains mandate information that's specific to that payment method.
* `upi` - See [`payment_method_details.upi`](#payment_method_details.upi) below.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.acss_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.acss_debit`

The `payment_method_details.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `default_for` - List of Stripe products where this mandate can be selected automatically.
* `interval_description` - Description of the interval. Only required if the 'payment_schedule' parameter is 'interval' or 'combined'.
* `payment_schedule` - Payment schedule for the mandate. Possible values: `combined`, `interval`, `sporadic`.
* `transaction_type` - Transaction type of the mandate. Possible values: `business`, `personal`.

<a id="payment_method_details.au_becs_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.au_becs_debit`

The `payment_method_details.au_becs_debit` attribute supports:

* `url` - The URL of the mandate. This URL generally contains sensitive information about the customer and should be shared with them exclusively.

<a id="payment_method_details.bacs_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.bacs_debit`

The `payment_method_details.bacs_debit` attribute supports:

* `display_name` - The display name for the account on this mandate.
* `network_status` - The status of the mandate on the Bacs network. Can be one of `pending`, `revoked`, `refused`, or `accepted`. Possible values: `accepted`, `pending`, `refused`, `revoked`.
* `reference` - The unique reference identifying the mandate on the Bacs network.
* `revocation_reason` - When the mandate is revoked on the Bacs network this field displays the reason for the revocation. Possible values: `account_closed`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `could_not_process`, `debit_not_authorized`.
* `service_user_number` - The service user number for the account on this mandate.
* `url` - The URL that will contain the mandate that the customer has signed.

<a id="payment_method_details.blik"></a>
### `payment_method_details.blik`

The `payment_method_details.blik` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - Date at which the mandate expires.
* `type` - Type of the mandate. Possible values: `off_session`.

<a id="payment_method_details.card"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card`

The `payment_method_details.card` attribute supports:

* `india` - See [`payment_method_details.card.india`](#payment_method_details.card.india) below.

<a id="payment_method_details.card.india"></a>
### `payment_method_details.card.india`

The `payment_method_details.card.india` attribute supports:

* `inactive_reason` - The reason why the mandate has an `inactive` status. This field is only populated if the mandate is inactive. Possible values: `canceled`, `card_not_supported`, `currency_not_supported`, `expired`, `issuer_not_supported`, `processing_error`, `undetermined`.

<a id="payment_method_details.paypal"></a>
### `payment_method_details.paypal`

The `payment_method_details.paypal` attribute supports:

* `billing_agreement_id` - The PayPal Billing Agreement ID (BAID). This is an ID generated by PayPal which represents the mandate between the merchant and the customer.
* `payer_id` - PayPal account PayerID. This identifier uniquely identifies the PayPal customer.

<a id="payment_method_details.payto"></a>
### `payment_method_details.payto`

The `payment_method_details.payto` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount that will be collected. It is required when `amount_type` is `fixed`.
* `amount_type` - The type of amount that will be collected. The amount charged must be exact or up to the value of `amount` param for `fixed` or `maximum` type respectively. Defaults to `maximum`. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `end_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, after which payments will not be collected. Defaults to no end date.
* `payment_schedule` - The periodicity at which payments will be collected. Defaults to `adhoc`. Possible values: `adhoc`, `annual`, `daily`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annual`, `weekly`.
* `payments_per_period` - The number of payments that will be made during a payment period. Defaults to 1 except for when `payment_schedule` is `adhoc`. In that case, it defaults to no limit.
* `purpose` - The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.
* `start_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, from which payments will be collected. Defaults to confirmation time.

<a id="payment_method_details.pix"></a>
### `payment_method_details.pix`

The `payment_method_details.pix` attribute supports:

* `amount_includes_iof` - Determines if the amount includes the IOF tax. Possible values: `always`, `never`.
* `amount_type` - Type of amount. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `end_date` - Date when the mandate expires and no further payments will be charged, in `YYYY-MM-DD`.
* `payment_schedule` - Schedule at which the future payments will be charged. Possible values: `halfyearly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `weekly`, `yearly`.
* `reference` - Subscription name displayed to buyers in their bank app.
* `start_date` - Start date of the mandate, in `YYYY-MM-DD`.

<a id="payment_method_details.sepa_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_details.sepa_debit`

The `payment_method_details.sepa_debit` attribute supports:

* `reference` - The unique reference of the mandate.
* `url` - The URL of the mandate. This URL generally contains sensitive information about the customer and should be shared with them exclusively.

<a id="payment_method_details.upi"></a>
### `payment_method_details.upi`

The `payment_method_details.upi` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount to be charged for future payments.
* `amount_type` - One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `description` - A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer.
* `end_date` - End date of the mandate or subscription.

<a id="payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `collection_method` - Mandate collection method Possible values: `paper`.

<a id="single_use"></a>
### `single_use`

The `single_use` attribute supports:

* `amount` - The amount of the payment on a single use mandate.
* `currency` - The currency of the payment on a single use mandate.
